items.title: James Hunter interviewed by Monk Rowe, Boston, Massachusetts, July 25, 2018
items.q: Duffy Power, he was another more obscure sort of British white soul singer, and he’d add his own little thing of strangeness to it.

ctx.x: Yeah, trying to get the same spirit of that and I think you can stultify something by trying to absolutely replicate it so I was trying to, I was trying to convey the same spirit. I always felt that for the most part, with a few exceptions that white America and British acts who attempted that style of music used to lose the finesse and they’d compensate by adding a bit more aggression. But the slinkiness, the sort of sinuous poetics of grace of the way the black performers used to do it I think was lost on a lot…
Were you compelled by, or suggested to by producers, like, “James if you just would do this we could sign you” or —
